summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.39/1717)

data.turoyo: U ḥa d muṭewolle huwanwo mamnun ġalabe mene.
data.translation: The one who obeyed them, they would be very pleased with him.

rationale: New Infectum-wa provisionally; contracted muṭe- and plural authority suffix with singular topic. Corrects reader Preterit-wa. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (Jan 3.6/69)

data.turoyo: Ba kṯawyoṯani kmaḥwe as səryoye mən greʕe maṭəʕone ne l Kamal w l Tərkiya.
data.translation: In these writings he shows the Syriacs as obedient servants of Kemal and Turkey.

rationale: New Part act. in -one; plural predication retains the l-authority construction. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New sense 2: unterwerfen, sich ein Land gefügig machen;

data.gloss: unterwerfen, sich ein Land gefügig machen;

rationale: Plural robbers are encoded by the agent suffix of maṭəʕʕe and u balad kule is a bare patient; this reverses the valency of obeying an l-marked authority. One attestation, with morphology to confirm.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.2/36)

data.turoyo: hani am mərdnoye, an noše d Mərde d mawballe i kalo kit baynoṯayye xayən masalan d lə kmaṭəʕənne, bale mi… m zuḥṯo lə kmaǧrən. <...>
data.translation: Die Leute von Mardin, diese Leute, die die Braut weggeführt hatten, unter ihnen waren auch Verräter, die (den Brüdern) nicht gehorchten, doch aus Angst wagten sie nicht .... <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum III.1: plural obeyers and suffixed plural authority.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.2/104)

data.turoyo: <...> mərre u ḥa d kəmaṭəʕ ṭər maṭəʕ, lə kmaṭəʕ hawxa w hawxa gəsaymina mene w mu babo. <...>
data.translation: <...> Wer sich unterwirft, der soll sich unterwerfen, und wer sich nicht unterwirft, mit dem und mit seinem Vater werden wir so und so verfahren. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum III.1: positive, bare after ṭər, and negative forms in one threat; count one context.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (56/71)

data.turoyo: Kul ḥa b mo gawre ne. Ksaymi ḥaramtiye bu balad, maṭəʕʕe u balad kule.
data.translation: Jeder von ihnen war so gut wie Hundert Mann; sie trieben das Räuberhandwerk im Lande und tyrannisierten das ganze Land.

rationale: First Preterit example of III.2, with overt plural agent morphology and country patient.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (64/176)

data.turoyo: Me d məlla l Gulčičaka Ǧənna, ǧbir u kačal, maṭəʕle lu mamrayḏa.
data.translation: Als Geisterrose so sprach, mußte der Kahlkopf ihrem Worte gehorchen.

rationale: Thin Preterit III.1: an l-marked utterance is obeyed, rather than an authority person.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (90/31)

data.turoyo: Hano koqoyəm, komaṭiʕo u=awro d u=gawrayḏa. Kmatəryole tre, tloṯo=zawge d ǧwerəx w kməlyo i=turkayḏe zuwade, tene w afšoṯe w laḥmo.
data.translation: Sie gehorcht dem Befehl ihres Gatten, weicht ihm zwei, drei schnürsohlen ein und füllt seinen Reisesack mit Wegzehrung, Feigen, Rosinen und Brot.

rationale: Thin Infectum III.1: bare nominal order complement, distinct from l-marked command/person.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (106/31)

data.turoyo: <...> "Ayna, d lo maṭi lu amro du greʕayḏi, lə gmaṭəʕ lu amrayḏi."
data.translation: <...> ‚Wer nicht dem Befehl meines Knechtes gehorcht, der ge- horcht meinem Befehle nicht.“

rationale: Fills Infectum III.1 to five contexts with a secure gmaṭəʕ and l-marked command. The preceding maṭi remains unresolved, not cited as evidence of a contracted ṭyʕ form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 3.15/180)

data.turoyo: Ḥa man noše, d hiw əšme b Awruppa lu qonṣoloṣ w li dawle d Tərkiya, Qašo Fəṭrus Šuše yo. Bəṯr mena, ʕal d lə maṭəʕle bu 'buyono' (!) du faṭəryarxo ste, ḥrim mi kohnuṯo m laf ḥasyo ʕIsa b Hollanda.
data.translation: One of the people whose name was given in Europe to the consul and the Turkish state is Father Petros Shushe. Afterwards, because he also did not comply with the patriarch's 'declaration' (!), he was excommunicated from the priesthood by Bishop Isa in Holland.

rationale: Thin Preterit III.1 after three contexts; b-marked normative declaration extends the command complement pattern. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: III.1 has authority persons in l-NPs or l-suffixes; commands can also occur in l-NPs or as a bare noun. Complement marking alone is not enough to establish III.2.

56/71 differs by the direction of control: the robbers impose submission on a country. The plural agent reading is morphologically plausible, and the active domination sense is marked as a one-token proposal.
The Arabic etymology is retained. These inflected Turoyo forms show lexical integration; no light-verb construction, Detransitive function or distinct contact-induced construction is established.
ṭər maṭəʕ in JTM 5.2/104 is a third-person dependent Infectum in a jussive context, not a second-person Imperativ.
Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals remain prior material and are not re-proposed here.
Jan political discourse gives obeyers, authorities and normative commands, not agents causing a country to submit. It therefore supports III.1 and does not independently confirm round-1 III.2.
maṭəʕone is a transparent -one agentive/qualitative plural, filed in Part act.; maṭiʕe could be a different adjective or contact form. Semantic obedience alone does not establish Part. Pass.
muṭewolle with singular u ḥa and plural authority suffix is provisionally Infectum-wa, distinct from suffixal-agent Preterit-wa. The contracted root shape warrants review.
Confirm maṭəʕʕe in 56/71 as plural-agent Preterit with u balad kule as patient; could speakers instead parse the country as an obeying participant? III.2 is based on one attestation.
Resolve maṭi in 106/31: a reduced maṭəʕ, transcription error, or mṭy construction? No new form is proposed.
Does l-marked versus bare command in 64/176, 90/31 and 106/31 reflect regular government variation or a dialect contrast? Current data do not decide.
Confirm contracted muṭewolle at Jan 1.39/1717 as Infectum-wa with authority suffix; a Preterit-wa reading would need a different account of singular u ḥa and -lle.
What is the paradigm/source of maṭiʕe at Jan 3.15/165: an adjective, Part act. variant or Part. Pass.? No new box is published for it.
Resolve suffix and number in maṭəʕʕe at Jan 2.16/3558 without deriving it from the English them.
Commands or words can be the obeyed complement: l-marked lu mamrayḏa/lu amrayḏi, or bare u awro. Same compliance meaning as obeying a person.
b-marked normative declaration and bu medano domain complement extend round-1 command/authority government. l- remains visible with personal/institutional authorities; no new compliance sense.
